cases.label: '' from a joined delivery method versus NULL from a NULL DeliveryMethodID in the same output column; SupplierReference NULL and '' the other way round
cases.reasoning: Supplier 3's delivery method exists and is named '' (DeliveryMethodName is NOT NULL, so '' is its only empty value); supplier 1's DeliveryMethodID is NULL, so the LEFT JOIN gives NULL in the same output column. SupplierReference is NULL on supplier 1 and '' on supplier 3, the reverse of the hand-derived case. A conversion that coalesced joined names to '', folded '' to NULL, or made the delivery-method join inner would differ. Every foreign key points at an existing row or is NULL.

cases.label: two suppliers share phone, fax and website; a NULL delivery method keeps its row; primary and alternate contacts are crossed
cases.reasoning: Suppliers 1 and 2 share PhoneNumber, FaxNumber and WebsiteURL (non-key ties; SupplierName stays unique as in the source). Supplier 2's DeliveryMethodID is NULL (a nullable foreign key), so the LEFT OUTER JOIN keeps it with a NULL method; an inner join would drop it. Supplier 1's contacts are persons 1 (primary) and 2 (alternate), supplier 2's the reverse, so a conversion that joined the alternate contact on the primary contact id would show the wrong names. All other foreign keys point at existing rows.
